To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1. Web page directories provide a cheap and easy way to label large sets of tweets; 2. Our proposed method for tweet classification achieves 82% of accuracy, performing only slightly worse than for web pages;

(1) we can infer tweet categories from web page directories with 82% accuracy; (2) the accuracy is comparable with that achieved for web page classification, which is a much easier task; and (3) our proposed method is inexpensive and easy to maintain, as it can be regenerated when new web page categories are created or old ones are removed

we propose a new model to label large sets of Twitter messages, which can be regenerated or updated at any time, and that our approach is able to achieve a classification performance comparable to that of web page classification.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: How can we automatically label large sets of tweets? What is the performance of our proposed model?
the following questions: How can we leverage the information contained in URLs to classify tweets? How can we use human-edited directories to label tweets?

the following questions: How can we leverage the information available in web page directories to automatically categorize tweets? What are the main challenges of such a task? What are the performance of the resulting classifiers?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we propose an effective method for the automatic labeling of large sets of tweets.

we propose a method for tweet classification that can be applied to large datasets with minimal human effort and with a high degree of accuracy, which is comparable to that achieved by state-of-the-art methods.
our proposed method is a cheap way to obtain a large set of labeled tweets, and can be used to bootstrap a classification model for tweets, or to improve an existing one.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we can use human-edited directories as an effective source of training data for large-scale classification tasks.
web page directories can be used to label a large amount of tweets, which is an inexpensive way for obtaining labeled data to train a tweet classifier.
we can now build large-scale classifiers for Twitter with a small effort and at a negligible cost.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of web page directories for tweet classification can help in the development of new applications that require a high level of automation.
the use of human-edited web directories is a promising way of generating training data for the classification of tweets.
, in the absence of large sets of labeled data, one can still use human-edited directories for classification.
